/record/summaryDescription	In the Qing dynasty (1644-1911) Jingdezhen potters experimented with new forms and glazes, often with support from the emperors and state officials. Chinese porcelain was admired and collected all over the world. The tradition of inscribing the emperor's reign title on the wares continued. The colour scheme on this bowl, with outlines painted in underglaze blue and the space within the outlines filled with coloured enamels, is called 'doucai'.
